newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds placed for rally if U.S. payrolls please.
newsitem.headline: Bunds placed for rally if U.S. payrolls please.

text.p: German debt prices clawed their way back into positive ground at the open on Friday, reclaiming some of the losses sustained in late Thursday trade.

Analysts said the main feature of the day would be the U.S. non-farm payrolls report, due at 1230 GMT. Until then, Bunds were likely to remain relatively subdued, but afterwards, the market could be sent to the upside, they said.
"Prices appear to be in a position to rally as long as bearish surprises can be avoided," analysts at DMG Futures and Options said in a morning note.

Economists polled by Reuters expect 193,000 jobs to have been added to the non-farm payroll in July, compared with 217,000 in July. The unemployment rate is expected to tick down to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent previously.
By 0650 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was trading unchanged on the day at 103.05, having made a more positive start to the session reaching a high at 103.15 after the open.

Technical analysts said any further weakening of prices would see the 103.00 to 102.91 support band into play, while sustained downward pressure would point towards the next support in th 102.68 to 102.71 area.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 103.37 for a bid yield of 5.540 percent by 0705 GMT.

The dollar, which had been stabilising over the past few sessions at around 1.83 marks, made another push to the upside in Tokyo overnight on talk of buy orders from U.S. funds. It was trading at 1.8460 marks in early European dealings.

Traders said the weakness of the mark would continue to play on market nerves amid speculation that any sharp turn for the worse in the mark's level might prompt the Bundesbank to tighten money market rates.
This would continue to weigh on the short end, they said.
